intro: In an analogy of figures, figure 1 changes into figure 2 by a rule. Find that rule, then make the same change to figure 3 and pick the figure it gives.

tips.title: Say the change in words
tips.body: Look at figure 1 and figure 2 and name every change: the outline, the shape inside, the number of dots or sides, the shading, and which way things point. Most book questions change 2 or 3 things at once.

tips.title: Follow one part when a figure turns
tips.body: Pick one part that is easy to spot, such as a black dot or an arrow, and see where it goes. A quarter turn clockwise moves the top to the right side, and the right side to the bottom.
tips.caption: Watch the black dot to see how far, and which way, the figure turns.

tips.title: Count the parts the shading moves
tips.body: In a circle or square cut into parts, count how many parts each shaded piece moves, and which way. Different pieces can move by different amounts.
tips.caption: Both shaded parts move 2 parts clockwise each time.

tips.title: Count sides and dots
tips.body: A triangle often becomes a square, and a square a pentagon: one more side. Count the dots in each part too, since 2 dots may become 3.

tips.title: Check every option against every change
tips.body: Wrong options usually get one change right and another wrong. Tick off each change you found against each option; only one option passes them all.
